clue.text: " We are seven ' the playmates might say

definitions.text: " We are seven ' the playmates might say

parts.words: " We are seven ' the playmates might say
parts.note: a group of seven children announcing themselves would call their group a set of seven, as a musical group of seven players is named

explanation.surface: A line from Wordsworth's poem about a child who insists her family numbers seven, put in the mouths of playmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We are Seven' is a Wordsworth poem; the clue pretends to quote it, but the playmates are 'players', and seven players together form a group named for the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of seven performers or items is a septet, from the Latin for seven.

clue.text: Where they keep drugs ? Then they'll be in the soup!

definitions.text: Where they keep drugs ? Then they'll be in the soup!

parts.words: Where they keep drugs ? Then they'll be in the soup
parts.note: read as a store of pot, cannabis, and as the kitchen vessel in which bones simmer for broth

explanation.surface: A remark that people hiding drugs are bound to land in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' is slang for cannabis and a stock is a supply, so a drug store; 'in the soup' means in trouble, but here it is literal broth.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pan in which bones and vegetables are simmered to make broth.

clue.text: Cash with an enclosed sign of atonement

indicators.note: cash with something enclosed holds it inside, so one piece goes into the other
cash with something enclosed holds it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: pence are British coins, small cash

explanation.surface: Money sent with an enclosed token of apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with an enclosed' puts AN inside PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of self-punishment shows sorrow for wrongdoing, a token of atoning.

clue.text: Sound hair-style for keeping in the waves

definitions.text: Sound hair-style for keeping in the waves

parts.words: Sound hair-style for keeping in the waves
parts.note: a 1920s hairstyle coiled over the ears, and devices that carry sound from radio waves to the ears

explanation.surface: A sensible hairdo that holds its waves in place.
explanation.walkthrough: The waves are radio waves as well as waves in hair; a style of plaits coiled over the ears was named after the listening device.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices worn on the head for listening to sound, also the name of an old coiled hairstyle.

clue.text: Branch that fails in its aims?

definitions.meaning: a side shoot growing from a main stem
something that shoots off target, missing what it aims at

explanation.surface: A description of a tree limb oddly accused of missing its targets.
explanation.definitionFit: A side growth from a main stem is an offshoot; read as 'off' plus 'shoot', it is a shot that goes wide.

clue.text: A Vatican sealer — or one's catchy clique?

definitions.meaning: the papal signet ring used to seal documents
an angler's circle of friends, catchy because they catch fish

explanation.surface: A puzzle over a papal seal and a gang of people good at catching things.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pope's signet ring shows St Peter fishing; 'catchy' in the second sense means good at catching fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's signet ring is named for St Peter the fisherman, and an angler's gang would be his circle.

clue.text: Capital embellishment backfires

indicators.note: the first part of the word backfires tells you the rest of it runs backwards

parts.note: the tail of the printed word backfires, split from its first part; the answer's reverse lies inside that word by coincidence of the split, not as a hidden word

explanation.surface: An ornate capital letter whose decoration goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfires' splits as 'back' plus 'fires': FIRES read backwards. 'Capital' is a capital letter, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stroke finishing a letter's lines decorates printed capitals.

clue.text: Heads this side

parts.note: a coin's face showing the head is its principal side

explanation.surface: A label marking which side of a coin is up.
explanation.walkthrough: The heads side of a coin has a technical name.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal face of a coin, bearing the head, as opposed to the reverse.

clue.text: Those who are 4 will not be on this

definitions.text: Those who are 4 will not be on this

parts.words: Those who are 4 will not be on this
parts.note: the 4 across answer, read as shots that go off, misses the mark it was aimed at

explanation.surface: A cross-reference saying certain people will be absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 across read as 'off shoot' is a shot that misses, so it is not on the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The mark a shooter aims at, which a stray shot misses.

clue.text: It shows very little consideration for the landlord

definitions.text: It shows very little consideration for the landlord

parts.words: It shows very little consideration for the landlord
parts.note: consideration is a legal term for payment; a nominal rent pays the owner almost nothing

explanation.surface: A complaint about a thoughtless tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consideration' looks like thoughtfulness, but in law it is the payment given under a contract; a nominal rent of a single peppercorn was traditional.
explanation.definitionFit: A token rent, traditionally one dried spice berry a year, paid to keep a lease valid.

clue.text: New losers can arrange to collect such strays

indicators.note: the losers can be rearranged, signalling that these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Unlucky people are told they can organise themselves to round up stray animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can arrange' tells you to rearrange NEW LOSERS; 'to collect' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are animals with no keeper, so they lack anyone to claim them.

clue.text: A wandering dog as an archery mark?

definitions.meaning: a dog that roams, and a common old dog's name
in archery a target chosen at random at an uncertain range is called by this name

explanation.surface: A question whether a roaming dog might serve as a target for archers.
explanation.walkthrough: In old archery, shooting 'at rovers' meant shooting at random marks of unknown distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A roaming person or animal is a rover, and archers once used the same word for a randomly chosen target.

clue.text: Crafty family association ?

parts.note: read 'crafty' as having to do with a craft or vessel: a family's boat, and also relatedness by blood

explanation.surface: A cunning clan banding together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' looks like 'cunning' but points to a craft, a ship, joined to a word for family.
explanation.definitionFit: Relationship by blood or family ties is kinship.

clue.text: Give effect to this in the kitchen for certain

indicators.note: 'this' is the answer, said to sit in the words that follow, so the letters run through them

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to carry something out in the kitchen without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across kitchEN FOR CErtain.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a law or rule take effect is to impose or apply it.

clue.text: Lyrical piece now showing at the cinema

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
a film now showing is said to be on

explanation.surface: A poem currently being screened at the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: Odeon is a well-known British chain of cinemas, and the name serves for a cinema in general.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odeon chain gave its name to picture houses generally in Britain.

clue.text: Horned beast summoned, having run amok

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep with horns
to page someone is to call for them over a public address

explanation.surface: A horned animal is called for after charging about wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging about violently and out of control is to have rampaged.

clue.text: Worthy of a male bird when ruffled

indicators.note: feathers that are ruffled are disordered, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Something deserving the attention of a cock bird with its feathers puffed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when ruffled' rearranges A MALE BIRD; 'of' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving praise or respect means worthy of admiration.

clue.text: Write a quotation on Washington's Defence Depart merit

definitions.note: the page prints Department split over a line, which the feed reads as two words; it means the US defence ministry

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tag is a familiar quotation or saying

explanation.surface: A request to put a quote onto the US military headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: A tag, as in a Latin tag, is a stock quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building outside Washington houses the US Department of Defense, and its name stands for it.

clue.text: For stirring up a storm?

parts.note: a storm in a teacup is a fuss over nothing; the small utensil that stirs a cup's contents could be said to stir one up

explanation.surface: A question about what would whip up a tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'a storm in a teacup' turns the storm into a cup of tea, which is stirred with a small kitchen implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The small implement used to stir a cup of tea.

clue.text: The way the world turns — could it be love?

parts.note: E stands for Earth, the world
turning is a form of movement

explanation.surface: Wondering whether love is what makes the world go round.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'love makes the world go round'; the way the world turns is the Earth's movement, E and MOTION. Love is one feeling among many, hence 'could it be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is an example of a strong feeling.

clue.text: Did Agag come so delicately to provide this meat for Samuel ?

definitions.text: Did Agag come so delicately to provide this meat for Samuel ?

parts.words: Did Agag come so delicately to provide this meat for Samuel
parts.note: in 1 Samuel 15 King Agag came to Samuel 'delicately', with small dainty steps, and was then hewn in pieces: both the walk and chopped meat

explanation.surface: A biblical question whether King Agag's dainty approach made him meat for the prophet Samuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Agag, king of the Amalekites, 'came unto him delicately' and Samuel hewed him in pieces: he walked with dainty steps and ended up chopped fine.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with small affected steps, and finely chopped meat, share one word.

clue.text: For the old golfer preparing to write his memoirs?

definitions.text: For the old golfer preparing to write his memoirs?

parts.words: For the old golfer preparing to write his memoirs
parts.note: an old-fashioned golf club, read as the golfer wetting his pen point with his tongue before writing

explanation.surface: A retired golfer getting ready to write his autobiography.
explanation.walkthrough: The old club reads as nib plus lick: licking a pen's nib was a writer's habit before starting.
explanation.definitionFit: An old iron golf club with a steeply angled face, roughly a modern nine iron.

clue.text: Big Ben, dismantled, leaving our shores

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart, so these letters are reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: London's great clock tower taken to pieces and shipped abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismantled' rearranges BIG BEN. 'Leaving our shores' looks like emigration, but it is the tide going out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide going out retreats from the coast.

clue.text: Fairman batting on a tightrope

definitions.note: the clue names the man by where he performed, a phrase standing for the performer

parts.note: printed as one word, a fair man: a fair-haired man is blond
a batsman batting in cricket is in

explanation.surface: A fair-haired man in at the crease, walking a tightrope.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Blondin was the French acrobat who crossed Niagara Falls on a tightrope; 'on a tightrope' points to him as the famous walker.
explanation.definitionFit: Blondin was the most famous tightrope walker of the nineteenth century, crossing Niagara Falls on a high wire.

clue.text: Where he takes courses in his training?

definitions.text: Where he takes courses in his training?

parts.words: Where he takes courses in his training
parts.note: courses are dishes of a meal and training is travelling by train: the dining car

explanation.surface: A question about where a student attends lessons during his training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' looks like study, but they are courses of a meal, eaten while travelling by train in the dining car.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway dining car, where passengers eat meals, and also someone who dines.

clue.text: Something the gunner and engineer got their teeth into?

definitions.text: Something the gunner and engineer got their teeth into?

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for a gunner
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for an engineer
to have got one's teeth into something is to have bitten it

explanation.surface: Two soldiers sharing a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the dish of melted cheese on toast is what the two soldiers bit. Welsh rarebit is a British cheese-on-toast dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit, melted cheese on toast, is a snack to bite into.

clue.text: Nine to one on — Firewheel Man

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Betting odds of nine to one on, quoted alongside a fiery wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine to one on' reads like betting odds; here it is just IX, I and ON in a row. In Greek myth Ixion was bound to a fiery wheel in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Zeus punished the king who desired Hera by binding him to a burning wheel for ever.

clue.text: French maid returning to fish, making one peer?

indicators.note: a thing returning comes back, so the word for the maid is read backwards

parts.note: bonne is French for a maid
a ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A French servant coming back to fish, which makes her the equal of anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns BONNE round to ENNOB. 'Peer' looks like the verb 'look', but here it is a member of the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the nobility makes them a lord or lady.

clue.text: Give birth to a teenager-that's wild!

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so these letters run in a new order

explanation.surface: Shock at a teenage pregnancy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's wild' rearranges TEENAGER; 'a' is link wording.
explanation.definitionFit: To produce or bring into being, as a parent produces offspring.

clue.text: Signal Brook forwards

parts.note: a beck is a northern English word for a stream
on means forwards, as in 'move on'

explanation.surface: An instruction to wave someone called Brook ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brook' looks like a name; it is a stream, BECK in northern English.
explanation.definitionFit: To summon someone with a gesture is to signal them over.
